title: 两家美国科技巨头助力沙特实现人工智能愿景
content:
Most AI infrastructure news arrives as a promise: a groundbreaking ceremony, a memorandum of understanding, a target date years out. This one arrived as a status update from a data center that is already turned on.
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), Cisco Systems (CSCO) and Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN said on Monday, August 31, that AI computing capacity built around AMD's Instinct MI355X chips and Cisco's networking hardware is now live in the kingdom, serving paying customers rather than sitting on a construction schedule.
That distinction matters, because most of the AI buildout headlines investors see this year describe plans and promises, not production.
Related: Nvidia's $96 billion quarter revealed a surprising constraint
The infrastructure is live, not just promised
The system running in Saudi Arabia combines AMD's Instinct MI355X graphics processors and EPYC server chips with Cisco's Silicon One networking chips and 800G optics, according to a joint statement from the companies.
HUMAIN, the AI arm of Saudi Arabia's roughly $1 trillion Public Investment Fund, is using the setup to sell GPU capacity to customers inside and outside the kingdom.
That capability did not exist ten months ago. AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN only announced their joint venture in November 2025, when they told Reuters the project had landed its first customer, generative-video startup Luma AI, for an initial 100-megawatt buildout.
Moving from announcement to live production workloads in under a year is fast by data center standards.
HUMAIN CEO Tareq Amin said the milestone "demonstrates HUMAIN's ability to build, operate and deliver advanced AI infrastructure at scale."
A second phase of up to 250 megawatts, using AMD's newer Instinct MI400 series chips, is due to begin deployment in 2027, with the joint venture still targeting up 1 gigawatt of capacity by 2030.
Saudi's chip supply still needs Washington's yes
The bigger story is what Monday's announcement does not mention: every future chip shipment still depends on individual U.S. export approval, so in a way, they need Washington's "YES".
Washington authorized HUMAIN to buy the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips back in November 2025, but that clearance came case by case, not as standing policy, according to the Commerce Department.

That gap widened in July 2026, when the Commerce Department moved the United Arab Emirates into Country Group A:5, the top tier of U.S. export trust, letting approved Emirati firms buy advanced AI chips without individual licenses.

report.summary: 美企助力沙特AI算力上线，芯片供应仍受美审批限制。
report.background: 沙特正通过约1万亿美元的公共投资基金大力押注AI，2025年成立AI公司HUMAIN，旨在将沙特打造为区域算力中心。2025年11月AMD、Cisco与HUMAIN宣布合资建设数据中心，如今已正式投产，速度超行业常规。然而，美国对先进AI芯片的出口管制仍是最大变量，沙特需逐案获批，而阿联酋已获更高待遇，凸显政策差异。
key_points: AMD、Cisco与沙特HUMAIN合建的数据中心已从图纸变为现实，使用AMD Instinct MI355X和Cisco网络硬件，为付费客户提供算力，首个客户是视频生成公司Luma AI。
项目二期将扩容至250兆瓦，采用AMD下一代MI400芯片，2030年总目标达1吉瓦，显示沙特大规模算力扩张的野心。
尽管算力已上线，但后续芯片发货仍需美国逐案出口许可，目前已获准采购相当于3.5万块Nvidia Blackwell芯片，但并非一劳永逸，供应链存在不确定性。
美国对中东AI政策分化：阿联酋获准无需个别许可即可购买先进芯片，沙特却被逐案审查，这种差别可能影响未来两国AI竞争力。
report.impact: 对AI行业，AMD在高性能计算领域进一步提升存在感，打破Nvidia垄断，中东成为算力出海新目的地。对开发者，可获取更多异构算力资源，但需遵守数据跨境与出口管制法规。对普通用户，AI视频生成等应用可能因本地算力加快落地，但也要关注规模化部署后的能耗与合规问题。
report.tools: 建议跟进AMD ROCm开源计算平台，用于在Instinct GPU上运行AI框架；Cisco Silicon One相关网络技术文档；可试用Luma AI的生成式视频API，体验由该算力驱动的应用。
